text:
claire: Quick sync — Legal asked for an OK on audit-log retention and consent/data-minimization for the upcoming enterprise pilot. Need to pick default retention, redaction approach, and how BYOK affects exports. cc @rakesh @devin @emily :eyes:
rakesh: TL;DR from infra: full raw logs are expensive and make queries slower. Recommend 3 buckets: 30d (hot), 365d (warm), archival cold (7y). Also suggest sampling + compacted indexes for long-term.
devin: +1 on buckets. For pilot I'd propose default 90d for standard tenants, enterprise opt-in to 1y, and ability to set tenant-level retention via console/API. Needs product + legal signoff.
emily: Legal: two concerns — 1) PII in logs (user email, IP) — we need mandatory redaction options, and 2) legal hold/ediscovery overrides that allow retention to exceed tenant setting. Also need exported evidence format to be auditable.
claire: Emily — what do you mean by "redaction options"? full removal vs hashing? Any must-haves?
emily: Hashing is ok for analytics, but for legal we sometimes need reversible mapping (escrowed key). So we need a configurable policy: redaction (irreversible), pseudonymize (hash), or reversible (tokenization with KMS-wrapped keys). Contractually reversible must be explicit in SLA.
mike: For BYOK: we can support envelope encryption where the customer's CMK wraps data keys. That works for reversible tokenization. Need to decide whether audit exports include plaintext for customers or always encrypted and we provide a decryption flow.
rakesh: Operationally, allowing reversible mappings increases attack surface. If we do it, require HSM-backed CMKs and rotation policies. Also note searchability: hashed IDs still allow joins but not lookups by original value unless we store a mapping.
devin: Proposed acceptance criteria for pilot: 1) tenant retention config API + console UI, 2) per-tenant redaction policy (redact/hash/reversible) with defaults, 3) BYOK option for reversible mode, 4) export tool that generates auditable evidence + manifest, 5) legal hold override flag visible in console and API.
sre-bot: deploybot: canary rollout for audit-redaction v1 scheduled for 2026-01-12 03:00 UTC.
emily: Need SOC2 mapping: which control covers audit retention + export? We want a mapping doc for the pilot. Also need to update DPA language for reversible exports & key escrow.
claire: Good call. Also product constraints: if we allow reversible mapping, feature should default off for self-serve. Only enabled for Reserved/Enterprise after paperwork.
mike: Implementation note: retention enforcement should be a background job that marks rows with removed fields rather than immediate deletion to avoid breaking queries/responders. We'll surface a delete API that triggers actual expiry.
rakesh: For cost: propose we implement lightweight compaction after 30d for hot->warm, then sampling for warm->cold. We can expose retention cost estimates in billing dashboard.
devin: UX notes: in console show "Retention policy" with quick presets (30/90/365/custom) and a toggle for "Redact PII" with dropdown for pseudonymize/reversible. Also show a "Request legal hold" button that creates an evidence ticket.
emily: Legal will provide suggested DPA wording & SOC2 mapping by EOW. Also we need runbook for responding to evidence requests (SLA, export format, signed attestations).
claire: Next steps/owners: Devin -> prototype API + console mockups (owner devin), Mike -> BYOK design and HSM requirements (owner mike), Rakesh -> retention compaction plan + cost model (owner rakesh), Emily -> DPA wording & SOC2 mapping (owner emily). I'll collect PRD draft by Friday. Anyone object?
rakesh: ACK. No objections.
mike: ACK. I'll add a short tech note on key escrow/security tradeoffs.
devin: ACK — will post mockups in #product-docs and link back here.
emily: ACK — will loop in legal counsel.
claire: Thanks all — I'll seed the PRD and tag owners. :thumbsup:
